legend: MRI of ischaemic fasciitis in a 91-year-old man with tender palpable mass on lateral aspect of right hip. An irregular mass is seen in the subcutaneous tissues over the right lateral hip abutting the underlying fascia (arrows), with low signal on the coronal T1-weighted image (shown here), intermediate T2 signal intensity on the coronal fat-saturated proton density–weighted image (Fig. <<38012>>), and corresponding enhancement with a central area of non-enhancing necrosis on the fat-saturated coronal T1-weighted image after gadolinium administration (Fig. <<38013>>). Biopsy confirmed ischaemic fasciitis.

Scattered aggregates and singly dispersed spindle cells with round to ovoid nuclei in a background of blood and granular debris (Pap).
Occasional aggregates of spindle and histiocytic cells, some with degenerative, dark, smudged nuclei (Giemsa).
CNB showing a zonal pattern, with a granulation tissue–like vascular proliferation that abruptly transitions to avascular fibrinoid necrosis (H&E).

Excisional biopsy demonstrating distinct zonation. The cellular region contains myxoid stroma with fibroblasts, myofibroblasts, vascular proliferation with hyalinosis of vessel walls, and extravasated erythrocytes. There is an adjacent region of hypocellular necrosis (H&E).
The cellular region demonstrates myofibroblasts with morphology ranging from spindle to stellate or ganglion-like (H&E).
